AGENDA 
 
Advisory Committee on Housing 
Thursday, November 19, 2026 
73 Harlow Street – Council Chambers 
Bangor, Maine 
5:00 PM 
 
 
1. Introductions 
 
2. Staff Review of Housing Efforts since 2019 
 
3. Discussion of Committee Goals, Responsibilities, and Staff Support 
 
4. Election of Officers – Chair, Vice Chair 
 
5. Set Next Meeting, Meeting Schedule, and Agenda Topics 
 
6. Adjournment
Anne M Krieg, AICP - Director 
 
Community & Economic Development 
Memorandum 
To: Advisory Committee on Housing 
From: Anne Krieg 
CC: Date: November 12, 2026 
Regarding: Introductions 
 
Please accept this memorandum as a welcome and introduction to the Committee.  On 
behalf of the City of Bangor, thank you in advance for serving on this crucial element of 
economic development and quality of life in the city.   
In your packet are the committee charge and the list of committee members.  Also 
placed in your packet is a staff presentation to orient members on what was 
accomplished since the last Affordable Housing Committee of 2018.   
If your schedule permits, or as you work with the committee, you are encouraged to 
review the plans and policy documents created and approved by previous City Councils 
regarding housing.  These plans and policies guide staff in our work. 
You can find those plans here:  https://bangormaine.gov/474/City-Plans 
Notably, I would encourage you to review the: 
 CDBG (Community Development Block Grant – HUD) Action Plan and 
Consolidated Plan 
 Comprehensive Plan 
 Economic Strategy Plan 
Also: 
 Housing: Bangor Affordable Housing Implementation Guide, 2025 (PDF) 
 Housing: Bangor Housing Study, 2025 (PDF) 
 Housing Workgroup Report and Recommendations (PDF) 
 
Understanding the last 7 years of work on housing, as well as current undertakings, 
coupled with a review of the plans and policies that guide our work, will help give the 
Committee a beginning framework to move forward.  This will also help with avoiding 
redundancies.
City of Bangor Community & Economic Development 
 
pg. 2 
 
I will serve as your point person for staff on the Committee.  Other members of my team 
in Code, Community Development, Economic Development, and Planning will support 
as needed.  Housing affects multiple disciplines, as you already know from your interest 
in serving this committee; you cannot have a conversation in Bangor without discussing 
housing. 
As you review these documents, you may want to think about seeking answers to these 
questions: 
 Do these plans and policies reflect housing needs in Bangor? 
 What else should city government focus staff/city funds on? 
 Moreover, generally, what is missing in this picture? 
Again, thank you for your service to the city in this capacity.  Please do not hesitate to 
email, call in advance of a meeting if you have questions, or need additional 
information.  We are here to help you make recommendations to the Council, backed by 
the best information, data, and professional practice.
